title: Model quantization and compatibility — customer readiness checklist & operator playbook
author: Ava Patel
content:
Overview

This page describes the customer-facing requirements and the operator runbook for performing model quantization and compatibility validation in Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. It covers acceptance criteria, staged rollout steps, preflight checks, monitoring thresholds, and explicit rollback triggers. The goal is to provide a repeatable, auditable process that protects customer SLAs and preserves model quality while enabling cost-efficient quantized execution on heterogeneous GPU/CPU fleets.

Scope

- Applies to model artifact updates that introduce any quantized weight formats (e.g., 8-bit, 4-bit, or mixed-precision) or kernel ABI changes that affect runtime compatibility.
- Targets Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). Hosted/Dedicated customers should reference the hosted quantization guidance instead.
- Intended audience: Field operators, SRE/Platform on-call, Solutions Engineers, and Customer Success engineers during handoffs.

Why this matters

- Quantization reduces memory and cost but can alter numeric characteristics and performance. A structured validation prevents regressions in latency, throughput, and output quality.
- Private deployments often contain heterogeneous accelerators (A100, H100, inferred ARM CPUs). Compatibility mismatches occur when kernels or compilation artifacts do not match target microarchitectures.

Acceptance Criteria (customer-facing)

Use the following acceptance thresholds for a quantized model variant to be considered "ready" for staged rollout to production tenants: 

1) Quality (functional):
   - Task accuracy / F1 / BLEU / ROUGE: not worse than baseline model by more than 1.5 absolute points for critical prompt set; or relative drop <= 3% if metric is ratio-based.
   - Latent semantic similarity (embedding-based): average cosine similarity to baseline embeddings >= 0.985 on the customer prompt set.

2) Latency and throughput:
   - p95 generation latency at customer sequence length baseline: increase <= 15% compared to baseline run.
   - Sustained throughput (tokens/sec) degradation <= 10% under the target batch profile.

3) Resource and thermal behavior:
   - GPU memory usage reduced as expected by quantization profile (documented in the quant-profile YAML).
   - No sustained thermal throttling or preemption events during synthetic burn-in runs.

4) Stability:
   - No hard crashes, CUDA driver errors, or kernel OOMs during a 4-hour burn-in with representative traffic.
   - KV-cache eviction patterns are compatible (see KV cache compatibility checklist).

Preflight checklist (operator)

- Operator ownership: assign a primary operator and a secondary on-call.
- Artifact verification: verify model bundle signature and provenance chain (SHA256 + cosign signature).
- Quantization profile: confirm quantization YAML is present and matches runtime capability matrix.
- Runtime compatibility table: confirm target runtime binaries (libredwood_runtime.so) and kernel variants are present for target hardware.
- Customer telemetry contract: confirm telemetry level required by customer (sampling rate, PII redaction) is enabled.

Minimum test matrix (must pass all items)

| Test case | Description | Acceptance |
|---|---:|---|
| Unit smoke | Load model, run a minimal token generation | returns tokens, no errors |
| Synthetic throughput | Run load generator (k6/locust) at target qps | throughput within 10% |
| 4-hour burn-in | Continuous traffic representative of production | no crashes, no OOM |
| Prompt-set regression | Run customer prompt set (50–200 prompts) | quality thresholds met |
| Embedding parity | 1000 sample vectors from customer corpus | cosine >= 0.985 |
| KV-cache survival | Warm cache then run eviction scenarios | no correctness issues |
| Telemetry sanity | Ensure traces, metrics, and logs emitted | sample rate observed |

Staged rollout plan (recommended)

1) Canary (internal): deploy quantized variant into an isolated canary tenant on the same hardware family.
   - Duration: 6–12 hours of synthetic + limited real traffic.
   - Validation: monitor latency p95, error rate, resource metrics.

2) Customer trial: enable quantized variant for 1–3 low-risk customer tenants with automatic fallback to baseline if metrics cross thresholds.
   - Duration: 24–72 hours.
   - Operators should run the prompt-set regression daily and compare results to baseline.

3) Gradual fan-out: increase tenant count by factors of 2 every 24 hours while monitoring.

4) Cutover: after 1 week of steady metrics, allow customer to opt in for full conversion. Maintain a 48-hour manual-backout window.

Operator rollout commands (examples)

- Verify artifact signature:

```
sha256sum model.quantized.tar.gz
cosign verify --key k8s://projects/redwood/keys/model-signing model.quantized.tar.gz
```

- Stage to canary runtime:

```
redwoodctl deploy model --bundle model.quantized.tar.gz --profile quant-profile.yaml --target canary-tenant --strategy staged
```

- Activate trial for customer tenant (example):

```
redwoodctl tenant set-model --tenant-id tenant-1234 --model-id model-v2-quant --rollout 10%
```

Rollback triggers and automation

Automated rollback should trigger when any of the following are observed for the affected tenant(s) within a 30-minute window unless overridden by a named approver: 

- p95 latency > configured SLO + 25% for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows.
- Error rate increase >= 1 percentage point and absolute error rate > 0.5% (application-level errors).
- Quality regression observed on daily prompt-set exceeding acceptance thresholds.
- Any hard runtime crash (segfault, driver panic, fatal kernel error).

Rollback steps (manual override)

1) Pause new traffic to the quantized variant: 
   - redwoodctl rollout pause --model model-v2-quant --tenant tenant-1234
2) Re-route traffic to previous model:
   - redwoodctl tenant set-model --tenant-id tenant-1234 --model-id model-v2-baseline --rollout 100%
3) Preserve artifacts and logs: collect model bundle, runtime logs, and kernel traces and attach to incident ticket.
4) If kernel/driver panic suspected, escalate to infra and file a field incident with detailed environment capture (dmesg, nvml logs, kernel oops)

KV cache compatibility notes

- Quantized models may change KV cache layout if activations are stored in lower precision. The runtime includes an on-disk compatibility tag at model bundle root: `kv_cache_compat: v2`. Operators must verify that target runtime supports the tag.
- If tag mismatch is detected, the runtime will refuse to mount existing cache by default; to preserve cold-start behavior, perform a warm-up pass to rebuild KV caches.

Quantization profile example (quant-profile.yaml)

```
model:
  name: model-v2
  variant: int8-quant
quantization:
  algorithm: blockwise-8bit
  per_channel: true
  calibration: dynamic
runtime_requirements:
  - kernel_variant: f16-accel-h100
  - min_compute_capability: 8.0
  - kv_cache_compat: "v2"
perf_expectation:
  p95_latency_pct_increase: 12
  throughput_drop_pct: 7
```

Telemetry & SLOs to monitor

- Metrics (emit at request-token granularity): request_latency_ms.p50/p95/p99, tokens_per_second, gpu_memory_bytes_total, kernel_errors.count
- Traces: sampling for cold-start request and first 10 tokens; attach model_id and quant_profile label.
- Logs: structured operation logs including artifact_sha, operator_id, tenant_id, node_id.
- Alert thresholds (suggested):
  - latency_p95 > baseline*1.25 -> Sev3 alert to oncall + operator
  - kernel_errors.count > 0 -> Sev2, immediate paging to infra
  - quality_regression.daily > threshold -> owner notification and ops review

Evidence for customer acceptance handoff

- Signed model bundle + checksum file.
- Burn-in run report (CSV) with latency, throughput, memory, and error metrics.
- Prompt-set regression report (diffs and sample outputs).
- Embedding parity report (summary stats and histogram).
- Telemetry contract verification (sampling rate and PII redaction snapshot).

Operator escalation matrix

1) Operator on-call (primary) — troubleshoot and execute rollback if needed.
2) Platform SRE — investigate kernel/driver failures.
3) Solutions Engineer (customer-facing) — coordinate customer communication.
4) Security/Legal (if telemetry/PII exposure suspected)

Postmortem and evidence preservation

- If rollback occurs, create a postmortem within 72 hours including timeline, root cause hypothesis, and mitigations. Attach: model bundle, runtime logs, kernel traces, alert graphs, and the acceptance test artifacts.

Appendix A — Example prompt-set regression runner (CLI)

```
# run prompt-set and produce CSV diff
python tools/prompt_regression_runner.py \
  --model-endpoint https://private-runner.local/tenants/tenant-1234/model-v2-quant \
  --prompts prompts/customer-critical-50.json \
  --output reports/quant_regression.csv
```

Appendix B — Common failure modes and mitigations

- Symptom: p95 latency spikes after quantized rollout.
  - Likely causes: suboptimal kernel variant selected, increased serialization overhead, or KV-cache rebuilds.
  - Mitigation: pin alternative kernel_variant in runtime config, increase batching window temporarily, or roll back.

- Symptom: embedding cosine drift below threshold.
  - Likely causes: calibration dataset mismatch or per-channel quantization error.
  - Mitigation: re-run calibration with customer corpus, increase calibration samples, or disable per_channel quantization.

- Symptom: GPU OOMs on some nodes only.
  - Likely causes: driver/kernel mismatch or firmware variation.
  - Mitigation: isolate affected nodes, run driver/firmware validation harness, move tenants off node.
